name: swedish_01
context: A tweet in Swedish, posted between April 2013 and February 2015 and collected through the Twitter Search API near the largest cities where the language is spoken. A native speaker labelled each tweet by the emotional attitude of the person who posted it.

versions.analysis_for_next: Neutral is the weakest class: only 81 of 189 gold-neutral texts were labelled neutral. 54 went to negative and 54 to positive. Too many texts were also pulled into neutral by mistake. Two parts of version 0 caused much of this. First, the rule that sharing bad news counts as negative. Gold-neutral headlines about Ebola, Kobane, a falling Eniro share and fas 3 criticism were all labelled negative. Second, the rule that mild friendly replies count as positive. Gold-neutral texts like 'Absolut. Jag förstår den ståndpunkten', 'önskar dig en god morgon' and auto-posts like 'Jag gillade ett videoklipp' were labelled positive. Political argument and campaign lines are mostly neutral unless they carry explicit emotion, yet the model labelled them negative. Disagreement or correction in a calm tone was also often gold neutral, so I am removing 'disagreement is negative'. Two other patterns are real. Sarcasm and irony ('Tur att bara tre av fyra laddplatser...upptagna', 'Ödmjukhet är mitt mellannamn') are negative, and the model labelled them positive. Explicit approval of a political act ('Är. Så. Bra.', 'Underbart attentat') is positive. Many errors look like label noise, so I will not chase those. The plan is to make neutral the default when emotion is not explicit, to drop the bad-news and mild-friendly rules, and to add a cue for sarcasm.

Version 1 pushed far too much into neutral. Negative recall fell from 156 to 97 and positive recall from 134 to 98, so macro-F1 dropped from 60.7 to 57.0. The errors show that these annotators read the poster's stance through what they choose to share. Retweets of political attacks (Björn Söder, SD, F!, Löfven gaffes), critical policy remarks, and news of harm (salmonella recall, abuse case, school decline, WWF warning) are mostly gold negative. Shares of good news, offers, events, tips and one's own side's achievements (free books, Sunday tip, more jobs since 2006, women on boards improving returns) are mostly gold positive. Sarcasm and pointed rhetorical questions to politicians are negative. Neutral is a smaller class: dry facts without good or bad valence, everyday questions and logistics, auto-posts ('Jag gillade ett videoklipp'), polite agreement, and some news headlines. So I am going back toward version 0's stance-by-content approach. I will keep version 1's gains: auto video likes and plain polite agreement stay neutral. I will tone down the version 0 swing in which every friendly reply was positive. Some errors are clear noise ('Sorgligt. Tack för allt' gold positive, 'Bästa appen' gold negative), so I will not chase them.

Version 2 (60.9) recovered negative and positive recall, but neutral recall fell to 69/189. Many gold-neutral texts are bare headlines and alerts (Ebola, Kobane, Tvärbanan stopp, Eniro), event listings, ads, job posts, auto video likes and calm corrections. Version 2 labelled these as negative or positive. Gold-negative shares usually expose wrongdoing or attack politicians. Gold-positive shares carry the poster's own endorsement. The plan is to keep the stance-through-sharing approach but route bare headlines, announcements, ads, auto-posts and calm corrections to neutral. This version is also trimmed to fit the 400-word limit.

Version 3 is the best so far (64.3), so I am keeping its structure and making small changes. Neutral is still the weakest class: 57 gold-neutral texts went to negative and 38 to positive. The neutral-to-negative errors are now mostly policy advocacy and campaign lines ('Högre lärartäthet...', 'S och MP måste få majoritet', 'Utred Nato', 'Dags för förändring'), election predictions ('Tvivlar på att FI kommer in'), and calm disagreement in replies. The neutral-to-positive errors include fan begging ('snälla följ mig'), check-ins ('Här står jag på en solterass'), auto video likes and mild personal remarks. The gold-negative political tweets that the model gets right mostly contain mockery, insults or exposure of a scandal. That lets me add one boundary: arguing for a policy, a campaign slogan or a prediction is neutral unless it mocks or condemns someone. Fan requests and check-ins also go to neutral. To stay under 400 words, I am swapping one neutral example for a campaign slogan rather than adding more text.

Version 4 (64.1) is level with version 3 (64.3). Neutral recall rose from 94 to 105, but negative recall fell from 165 to 154 and positive recall from 131 to 127. The new negative-to-neutral errors are political tweets that criticise opponents' policies or society in a calm tone: 'Väldigt många som röstar rött är för ROT men mot RUT', 'patriarkatet är inte längre aktuellt', 'Kamp EMOT nationalism', the BDS boycott and the akassa question. Version 4's policy-argument rule is too broad. Gold-neutral political texts mostly advocate the poster's own proposal or make a prediction. The ones gold marks negative mostly dispute or fault someone else. I will split the rule on that line: advocacy, slogans and predictions are neutral, while criticism of opponents, policies or society is negative. Positive recall also suffers on enthusiastic self-promotion ('Ikväll sparkar EM-kvalet igång!', 'SKRIV PÅ!!!!', 'Kom och häng', 'Nybloggat: Alla kan vara kreativa!'), which went to neutral. I will treat enthusiastic invitations and promotions as positive and leave only plain listings neutral. Headline noise (Ebola neutral vs salmonella negative) looks like a coin flip, so I am keeping version 3's handling. I am trimming wording elsewhere to stay under 400 words.

Version 5 scored 64.3, level with version 3, so these are small, targeted changes. Many positive-to-negative errors are playful texts that contain negative words: self-mockery with haha/hehe, teasing ('Jag retas bara!') and gloating over an opponent's setback. Version 5's 'Kom!' cue also pulled organisational invitations into positive, although gold labels them neutral. Gold-positive promotions show the poster's own excitement instead. The changes are: drop 'Kom!', make organisational announcements neutral, and make playful teasing, self-mockery and gloating positive. This version is trimmed to fit under 400 words.

Version 6 scored 64.4, roughly level with versions 3 and 5, so the gains now come from fine-tuning boundaries. The teasing and self-mockery rule raised positive recall from 125 to 134, but neutral-to-positive errors grew from 34 to 43. Most of the new ones are chatty replies where a passing 'haha', 'ha!', ':)' or '🙈' sits inside a mainly informational message or question: 'Har hört rykten! :) Finns tidn. att köpa i butik?', 'ha! Sitter redan på den f-linan', 'Jodå det är kul! ... Hur går det för dig??', 'Hah. En gammal klasskompis är med'. Gold labels these neutral. Gold-positive teasing makes the fun or affection the whole point ('Jag retas bara!'). So I will add a boundary: a passing laugh or smiley in a reply that mainly informs or asks is neutral. Positive needs warmth, praise, excitement or deliberate play as the main message. The Lean Coffee example is now classified correctly, so I am swapping it for the ':)'-with-question example to teach this boundary, and keeping organisational announcements in the neutral description. Political and headline noise stays as it is.
next_examples_not_copied: @stefanlundell @HNilsonne @karinbogren @danouc @CWalerud @Volumental Har hört rykten! :) Finns tidn. att köpa i butik? (Have heard rumours! :) Can the magazine be bought in shops?)

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 7 dropped to 61.5. The rule keeping a passing haha or :) neutral cut positive recall from 134 to 109 and barely helped neutral (98 to 105), so I am reverting it. Version 6 (64.4) is the best version, and versions 3 through 6 sit on a plateau around 64, which suggests heavy label noise. So version 8 returns to version 6 with one low-risk addition. Across every version, gold-positive shares framed as recommendations or free offers keep landing in neutral: 'Söndagstips! ... Fri entré!', 'Kostnadsfri e-bok', 'Värt att testa', 'Intressant om Kyros', 'Nybloggat: Alla kan vara kreativa!'. I will add recommendation cues (tips, värt att, intressant, fri entré) to positive. Plain organisational announcements without such framing stay neutral. I am trimming the positive description to stay under the word limit.

Version 8 is the best so far (64.7), and versions 3 to 8 sit on a plateau, so I am making only one targeted fix. Automatic 'Jag gillade ett videoklipp' posts with upbeat video titles are still labelled positive with high confidence. The rule now says outright that they are neutral whatever the title. I dropped two redundant cues and shortened one phrase to stay under 400 words.

Version 9 scored 64.3, slightly below version 8 (64.7), so the extra auto-post wording and the dropped cues did not help. Even 'I GOT A PUPPY!' stayed borderline. This is the last version, and versions 3 to 9 have all landed between 64.1 and 64.7, so the remaining errors look mostly like annotator noise. The safest final choice is to restore version 8 exactly, the best-scoring version. Its main rules are: stance shown through sharing, criticism of opponents counts as negative, own-side advocacy and uncommented headlines count as neutral, teasing and gloating count as positive, and recommendations and free offers count as positive.
